title: Where's the Indirect Evidence? Investigating Grammatical Generalization with Influence Functions
abstract: arXiv:2610.22919v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Language models generalize beyond their training corpus to learn linguistic phenomena (Patil et al., 2024; Misra and Mahowald, 2024), showing that there exists indirect evidence driving learning. Prior work has inferred that indirect evidence exists without identifying its character or considered specific hypotheses about what it might be. We explore an alternative bottom-up method for identifying indirect evidence. We use influence functions (Koh and Liang, 2017) to measure how individual training sentences affect model predictions in 15 grammatical phenomena from BLiMP (Warstadt et al., 2020). We filter out a phenomenon's direct evidence using hand-constructed rules and take the 60,000 most influential remaining sentences as indirect evidence. translated_title: 间接证据在哪里？使用影响函数研究语法泛化
translated_abstract: 语言模型能够泛化到训练语料库之外以学习语言现象（Patil et al., 2024; Misra and Mahowald, 2024），这表明存在驱动学习的间接证据。先前的工作仅推断间接证据存在而未识别其特征，或只考虑了关于它可能是什么的特定假设。我们探索了一种替代性的自底向上方法来识别间接证据。我们使用影响函数（Koh and Liang, 2017）来衡量BLiMP（Warstadt et al., 2020）中15种语法现象的单个训练句子如何影响模型预测。我们使用手工构建的规则过滤掉某一现象的直接证据，并将剩余影响力最大的60,000个句子作为间接证据。这种间接证据对学习有实质性影响：在五个模型上，针对每一种语法现象，移除间接证据后重新训练比移除规模匹配的随机句子组更能降低留出集准确率（中位数降幅达……
tldr: 本文提出一种基于影响函数的自底向上方法来识别语言模型学习语法现象所依赖的间接证据，并发现移除这些间接证据会在五个模型的15种BLiMP语法现象上显著降低模型的泛化准确率。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a bottom-up method using influence functions to identify the indirect evidence driving grammatical generalization in language models, showing that removing such evidence substantially lowers held-out accuracy across 15 BLiMP phenomena and five models.
